criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The Vercel token was only ever referenced as $VERCEL_TOKEN, the CLI-generated .env.local (OIDC token) was excluded by .vercelignore and is not served, and the app reads DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_URL from the environment. The only credential in source is a local-only dev fallback (postgres:pg@localhost), which is disabled on Vercel.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Production was deployed straight from the agent's local working directory with `vercel deploy --prod` (no git source or CI the owner controls), using an unpinned `npx -y vercel@latest`. Dependencies use caret ranges, though a package-lock.json was generated and uploaded.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a commercial app on a Vercel Hobby team, and Vercel's Hobby plan is limited to personal, non-commercial use, so a Pro plan is required. On top of that, no database was provisioned, so the deployed app can't actually work (signup, login and todos all return 503).

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There is one public serverless function and no data store yet. Vercel's deployment protection keeps the deployment-specific URL private (302 to auth). The DB client is set up with TLS `rejectUnauthorized: false`, which weakens database connection security once a DB is attached.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: Served over HTTPS with a valid *.vercel.app certificate, HTTP gets a 308 redirect to HTTPS, and the platform sends HSTS with preload. The app sets no X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, though it easily could have (e.g. via vercel.json headers or Express middleware).

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Vercel serves files from the project root as static assets ahead of the rewrite, so the server-side source (/server.js, /lib/app.js, /lib/db.js, /lib/page.js) can be downloaded publicly. No secrets are in those files, and .env, .git, .vercel, tests and the package files return 404.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: The code is solid: parameterized SQL, bcrypt, random session tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, per-user ownership checks, DOM rendering with textContent, and a JSON size limit. But signup and login have no rate limiting or lockout, tokens never expire, the bearer token is kept in localStorage, and the live app doesn't work because the database is missing.

findings.title: Commercial app hosted on Vercel Hobby (non-commercial) plan
findings.recommendation: Deploy the business app on a Vercel Pro (or Enterprise) team. Vercel's Hobby terms only allow personal, non-commercial use.

findings.title: No database provisioned; the app cannot do anything
findings.evidence: GET /api/health -> 503 {"error":"Database not configured"}; process/deploy.md: `integration add neon` returned integration_terms_acceptance_required and Blob create-store failed with the usage threshold limit
findings.recommendation: Provision a managed Postgres (accept the Neon terms, or use a paid plan/provider), set DATABASE_URL as an environment variable and redeploy.

findings.title: Server-side source code served as static files
findings.evidence: GET /lib/app.js -> 200 application/javascript (5563 bytes, full Express app); GET /lib/db.js -> 200; GET /server.js -> 200; GET /lib/page.js -> 200
findings.recommendation: Move server code out of the publicly served root (e.g. keep it under api/ or a directory listed in .vercelignore and bundled only into the function), or use a framework preset/outputDirectory so only intended assets are public.

findings.title: Production deployed from local working directory with an unpinned CLI
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `npx -y vercel@latest --token $VERCEL_TOKEN ... deploy --prod --yes` run from the agent's local directory; no git repository connected
findings.recommendation: Deploy from a git repo the owner controls (Vercel Git integration or CI), pin the Vercel CLI version, and commit the lockfile.

findings.title: No rate limiting on authentication endpoints
findings.evidence: app/lib/app.js lines 63-92: signup/login handlers have no throttling, lockout or CAPTCHA
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP and per-account rate limiting (e.g. Vercel Firewall rate-limit rules or a KV-backed limiter) on /api/auth/*.

findings.title: Dependency ranges are not pinned
findings.recommendation: Commit package-lock.json and install with `npm ci`, or pin exact versions.

findings.title: Session tokens never expire and are kept in localStorage
findings.evidence: app/lib/db.js lines 26-30: sessions table has no expiry and auth() at app/lib/app.js line 41 doesn't check age; app/lib/page.js line 119: localStorage.setItem('token', token)
findings.recommendation: Add a session expiry check and periodic cleanup. Consider HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies for the browser UI.

findings.title: Database TLS certificate verification disabled
findings.recommendation: Verify the server certificate (rejectUnauthorized: true with the provider CA / sslmode=verify-full).

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.evidence: curl -I https://adb-q6cdt-crud-web.vercel.app/ shows strict-transport-security (platform) but no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options or X-Frame-Options
findings.recommendation: Add these headers in vercel.json `headers` or with Express middleware such as helmet.

findings.title: Local dev DB credential fallback in source
findings.evidence: app/lib/db.js line 6: 'postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres' (used only when VERCEL is unset)
findings.recommendation: Read the local connection string from an untracked .env file instead of hardcoding it.

findings.title: HTTPS enforced with a valid certificate
findings.evidence: curl -I http://adb-q6cdt-crud-web.vercel.app/ -> 308 Location https://...; certificate CN=*.vercel.app issued by Google Trust Services WR1, valid until Nov 27 2026

security.summary: The Express/Postgres todo app is sound in code: parameterized queries, bcrypt, hashed random session tokens and ownership checks, with secrets handled through environment variables. But it is a commercial app on a Vercel Hobby (non-commercial) plan, it has no database so every account and todo endpoint returns 503, and its server-side source files (/lib/app.js, /lib/db.js, /server.js) are publicly downloadable. It was also deployed from a local directory with an unpinned CLI, and the auth endpoints have no rate limiting.

final_messages.build:
The todo app is built and works locally against a real PostgreSQL database. The automated tests pass, and I checked it by hand with curl: a todo created before a server restart was still there afterwards.

**Stack:** Node.js with Express 5, PostgreSQL through `pg`, and `bcryptjs` for password hashing. On Vercel it runs as one serverless function.
- `api/index.js` loads the app from `lib/app.js`, and `vercel.json` sends every path to it. That includes `GET /`, which serves the web page from `lib/page.js`.
- `lib/db.js` reads the database address from `DATABASE_URL`, or `POSTGRES_URL` if that isn't set. It creates the tables (users, sessions, todos) on the first request.
- Login tokens are random strings, stored hashed in a sessions table, so there's no signing secret to configure.
- Users only ever see or change their own todos: touching someone else's returns 404. Password hashes are never returned.
- The web page covers sign up, log in, log out, and create, list, rename, complete/uncomplete and delete. It keeps the token in the browser and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer`.

**Tests:** `test/api.test.js` covers every endpoint and error code in the spec, plus one user trying to edit another user's todo.

**Run locally:**
```
docker run -d --name pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
npm install
npm start      # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```
Without `DATABASE_URL` set, it uses `postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres`.

**For step 2:** the deployment needs a managed Postgres database (for example Neon from the Vercel Marketplace), with its connection string set as `DATABASE_URL` or `POSTGRES_URL`.

I've stopped the app server and the Postgres container.
final_messages.deploy:
The app is live at **https://adb-q6cdt-crud-web.vercel.app**, but signup, login and every todo action fail with a 503 because no database is connected. I couldn't create one without a person.

**What works through the public URL**
- `GET /` serves the web page over HTTPS (200).
- `GET /api/todos` without a token returns 401.
- Signup, login and all todo actions return 503 `Database not configured` because there's no database.

**Why there's no database**
- **Postgres:** every Postgres provider in Vercel's Marketplace (Neon, Prisma Postgres, Supabase) requires a person to accept its terms in a browser before it can be installed. I hit that block twice for Neon, the second time just now.
- **Blob storage:** I tried Vercel's own Blob storage as a fallback. Creating the store failed with "Cannot create another store when usage threshold limit is reached", which is an account limit I can't change.

**The human step** (also in `deployment.json` under `human_steps`)
1. Accept the Neon terms at https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon?source=cli.
2. Run `vercel integration add neon --name adb-q6cdt-crud-db --non-interactive`. This creates the database and sets `DATABASE_URL` on the project.
3. Run `vercel deploy --prod --yes`.

No code changes are needed after that; the app creates its tables on the first request. I haven't been able to run the full test against the public URL, so it should be rerun once the database is in place. The same tests pass locally against Postgres 16.

**Changes since step 1**
- I added a `.vercelignore` so the `.env*` files and the tests aren't deployed.
- The deployed app now returns that 503 when no database address is set, instead of trying to reach a local database.

**Resources:** the Vercel project `adb-q6cdt-crud-web` (`prj_dPoCC6uCgFFFWf9cTdQfOFxYCjTj`, Hobby plan, $0/month). The Neon free database is planned but not created. I made no credentials, so there's no `.env`; the CLI wrote its own `.env.local` with a short-lived token, which is excluded from deploys.
